item.title: Sphera Media Lab 2026: Open Call for Masterclasses and Keynotes
item.description:
Organisation: European Lab (Arty Farty) and the Sphera Network, coordinated by Medianes

Location: LaVallee, Rue Adolphe Lavallee 39, 1080 Brussels, Belgium. Proposals are accepted regardless of where you are based, but they should reflect a European perspective.

Award: Selected contributors receive a fee plus travel to Brussels and accommodation, all covered by the organisers. The fee amount is not published in the call. No submission fee.

Duration: One-day event on 3 December 2026; contributors deliver a single masterclass or keynote

Deadline: 31 Aug 2026

European Lab and the Sphera Network are opening submissions for the discourse programme of the next Sphera Media Lab, the annual forum for people defending independent media in Europe. THEMES: technological independence (sovereignty, tools, mutualisation); economic independence (cooperative models); editorial independence (press freedom, resisting the far right). FORMATS SOUGHT: masterclasses, led by an expert sharing advanced knowledge, technique and hands-on insight; and keynotes, inspiring talks grounded in a specific case study. WHO CAN PROPOSE: media outlets, associations, researchers and professionals. The organisers state they pay particular attention to parity and diversity across their programmes and ask that proposals take those criteria into account. WHAT IS COVERED: selected contributors travel to Brussels with transport, accommodation and a fee covered. THE EVENT: Sphera Media Lab 2026 runs on 3 December 2026 at LaVallee in Brussels, a full day of conferences, masterclasses and workshops for independent media professionals from across Europe, alongside the premiere of a documentary on threats facing European journalists. APPLICATION: submit your masterclass or keynote proposal via the Typeform at arty-farty.typeform.com/to/xnDikGGM before 31 August 2026.

item.title: Rory Peck Trust: Crisis Fund for Freelance Journalists
item.description:
Organisation: Rory Peck Trust

Location: Remote (worldwide); London-based organisation supporting freelancers anywhere

Award: Individual emergency grants; amounts are set case by case from an assessment of circumstances and need. No application fee.

Duration: One-off emergency assistance; assessment takes roughly one to three weeks

Deadline: Rolling / undated

The Rory Peck Trust's Crisis Fund gives direct financial assistance to freelance news journalists whose work has put them in crisis: physical attack, urgent medical costs, replacement of confiscated or destroyed equipment, forced relocation, or support for the family of a journalist who has been injured, imprisoned, kidnapped or killed. This is one of the few funds built specifically for freelancers working in conflict and high-risk environments, who are usually outside any staff safety net. ELIGIBILITY: professional freelance journalists in news and current affairs whose sole income comes from journalism, who have been working freelance for at least the last 12 months and can provide reference letters from editors, who have no access to other financial or government support and no contractual benefits such as sick pay or social security. The crisis must have happened within the last six months and must be evidenced (invoices, bank statements). Anyone who received Rory Peck Trust support in the last three years is ineligible. The Trust also runs a separate Therapy Fund and a HEFAT safety-training fund. Applications are rolling, in English, French, Arabic, Spanish, Ukrainian or Russian. Contact assistance@rorypecktrust.org or info@rorypecktrust.org.

item.title: Fonds BJP: Dossiersubsidie for Freelance Regional and Local Journalists (autumn 2026 round)
item.description:
Organisation: Fonds Bijzondere Journalistieke Projecten (Fonds BJP)

Location: Netherlands; for freelance journalists working on Dutch regional and local reporting

Award: Up to EUR 19,200 for six months of work on a single reporting dossier. No application fee.

Duration: Six months of dedicated reporting on one subject area

Deadline: 14 Sep 2026

The Dossiersubsidie is the Fonds BJP scheme for freelance regional and local journalists in the Netherlands who want to follow one subject properly rather than chase daily news, funding up to EUR 19,200 for six months of sustained reporting on a single dossier. It is aimed at the gap left by shrinking regional newsrooms, where structural coverage of local government, housing, care or industry rarely gets paid time. ELIGIBILITY: freelance journalists working in Dutch regional and local media only (staff journalists and national-only reporters are directed to the fund's other schemes). The fund also runs a year-round Vooronderzoekssubsidie of up to EUR 8,800 for preliminary research and a year-round Uitvoeringssubsidie of up to EUR 38,600 for carrying out projects, both open to all journalists. APPLICATION WINDOW: 17 August to 14 September 2026, via the Fonds BJP subsidy portal. Online office hours on 8 September 2026; questions on 020 63 86 295.

item.title: University of Twente: Postdoc, Ethics and Epistemology of LLMs4EU (17 months)
item.description:
Organisation: University of Twente, Philosophy section / 4TU.Center for Ethics and Technology

Location: Enschede, Netherlands

Award: EUR 4,241 to 5,538 gross per month (scale 10, steps 4 to 12) at 1.0 FTE, plus 8 percent holiday allowance and an 8.3 percent year-end bonus.

Duration: 17 months, full-time (38 to 40 hours per week), with possible extension

Deadline: Closed 25 Aug 2026

A postdoctoral position in the Philosophy section at the University of Twente, part of the 4TU.Center for Ethics and Technology, working on the ethics and epistemology strand (Work Package 6) of LLMs4EU. LLMs4EU is a European Commission funded initiative led by the Alliance for Language Technologies, spanning more than 20 countries, to build large language models across all EU languages and preserve European linguistic and cultural diversity in the digital age while keeping the resulting tools compliant with European values and legislation including the AI Act and the GDPR. TASKS: establish benchmarking frameworks that address legal and ethical concerns; develop guidelines for fine-tuning processes with an emphasis on preserving cultural heritage; oversee ethics compliance and advise the project ethics board; and build frameworks that integrate ethical considerations into LLM design. This is the tech-communication and language-politics end of AI research rather than a modelling job: the questions are whose language, whose culture and whose norms get encoded when a continent builds its own models. REQUIREMENTS: a doctorate in ethics, philosophy, science and technology studies, AI ethics, computer science with an ethics focus, or a related field; demonstrated expertise in AI ethics and ethics compliance; understanding of AI tool design and LLM development; appreciation for cultural diversity; strong communication and organisational skills; and professional English. Apply through the AcademicTransfer posting. Closes 25 August 2026.

item.title: Sundance Institute: Episodic Program and Lab 2027
item.description:
Organisation: Sundance Institute

Location: Open to international and U.S. applicants. In-person Lab takes place in the Atlanta, Georgia area, USA in Spring 2027; the Intensive track is fully online.

Award: No stipend or honorarium for participation. For the in-person Lab, Sundance covers round-trip basic economy airfare from the airport nearest the fellow's residence, shared housing with a private room and bath, and ground transport to and from the airport (fellows within 100 miles of the Lab get ground transport only). Meals, in-room charges, travel insurance, luggage fees and taxes are the fellow's own cost. One selected project also receives a separate monetary grant from the Alfred P. Sloan Foundation for a series with an illuminating emphasis on science, including medicine, energy, technology or invention. APPLICATION FEE: USD 50 nonrefundable processing fee per project submitted.

Duration: In-person Lab in Spring 2027 (event dates 15 to 20 April 2027) preceded by virtual workshops; the Intensive track convenes virtually in Summer 2027.

Deadline: Closed 25 Aug 2026

The Sundance Institute Episodic Program is an entry point for emerging to mid-career writers and creators working across all scripted series platforms, combining a lab experience with customised support to move projects and careers forward. The Episodic Lab lets writers workshop an original pilot and develop their writing and pitching skills: working with showrunners, producers and executives, fellows take part in one-on-one story meetings, pitching sessions, craft workshops and writers rooms. Up to ten applicants are selected, either for the in-person Lab (preceded by virtual workshops) or for a fully virtual Intensive with a creative advisor. ELIGIBILITY: applicants must be 18 or older; the script must be the applicant's original creation or adapted from optioned source material and written in English; the draft must be revised or new, not already produced, not sold to a third party and not distributed online; and applicants cannot have previously had an episodic project (pilot or pitch) produced by a studio or network. Open to international and U.S. participants, subject to travel guidelines. Up to two writers per project may participate, with one named as primary applicant. APPLICATION: submitted via FilmFreeway, including writer bios (250 words each), a series logline (50 words), pilot synopsis (500 words), one-page series overview (500 words), personal statement (250 words), community connection, thematic statement (250 words), characters and core relationships (250 words), episodic vision, optional video samples (up to three links, 10 minutes total), and the full pilot script as a PDF in standard screenplay format. Demographic questions are optional and do not affect consideration. Candidates may submit up to three applications, with a separate application and USD 50 fee for each project. Submissions opened 13 July 2026 and close 25 August 2026 at 6:00 p.m. PT. Finalists are notified by email through FilmFreeway around mid to late March 2027 (FilmFreeway lists 31 March 2027), and the list of selected writers and projects is published at sundance.org/epi after 15 April 2027. Finalists must return a Fellow Agreement, a Participation Agreement and any other required documents within five days. Questions: episodicprogram@sundance.org.

item.title: ProPublica Emerging Reporters Program 2026-2027
item.description:
Organisation: ProPublica

Location: Remote, with an all-expenses-paid trip to a journalism conference. RESTRICTED: US citizens or US residents only, and participants must supply a completed W-9 with a valid SSN or ITIN (no exceptions).

Award: $9,000 stipend, paid as two instalments of $4,500 (one at the start of the programme, one at the midpoint), plus a fully funded journalism conference trip with accommodation and expenses covered. No application fee.

Duration: Late September 2026 through June 2027, remote

Deadline: Closed 17 Aug 2026

ProPublica's Emerging Reporters Program is a remote mentorship and professional-development programme for aspiring investigative journalists, built specifically for students for whom investigative journalism is financially out of reach. Five students are selected each year. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $9,000 stipend paid in two $4,500 instalments (start and midpoint), one-to-one mentoring from ProPublica journalists, training and resources, and an all-expenses-paid trip to a journalism conference such as the Investigative Reporters and Editors conference (accommodation and expenses covered by ProPublica). ELIGIBILITY: undergraduate juniors or seniors enrolled during the 2026-27 academic year, who can demonstrate financial need and early dedication to journalism through internships, campus publications or local news work. Students from groups traditionally underrepresented in journalism are especially encouraged to apply. HARD RESTRICTION: applicants must be US citizens or US residents and able to file US taxes; the required W-9 needs a valid Social Security number or ITIN, and ProPublica states it makes no exceptions. APPLICATION: resume or CV, current academic transcript, expected graduation date, essays on investigative-journalism interest, career goals, financial circumstances and barriers faced, plus three journalism projects with URLs or PDFs and a backstory of up to 200 words each. Applications close 17 August 2026 at 9:00am ET.

item.title: Trusted Creator Fellowship 2026 (News Creator Corps)
item.description:
Organisation: News Creator Corps (a project of the Good Information Foundation)

Location: Virtual, meeting once a week. RESTRICTED: US-based creators only.

Award: $5,000 stipend on completing the programme. No application fee.

Duration: Roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026, virtual sessions once a week

Deadline: Closed 17 Aug 2026

A short-term virtual fellowship from News Creator Corps that trains independent content creators in the tactical craft of journalism: fact-checking, sourcing and interviewing, applied directly to their own channels during the programme so the community they already serve gets more credible information. WHO IT IS FOR: independent creators with an engaged following on digital platforms (Instagram, TikTok, Twitch, Substack, YouTube and similar) whose content is information-based and serves a specific community. It is explicitly not aimed at traditional journalists already trained in reporting fundamentals. STUDENT SEATS: three places in the autumn cohort are reserved for full-time college students aged 25 or younger, who get the same fellowship experience as everyone else. WHAT FELLOWS RECEIVE: a $5,000 stipend on completion, weekly virtual sessions, and access to discussion forums with the cohort, trainers, staff and alumni. ELIGIBILITY: US-based only. KEY DATES: applications close 17 August 2026 at 11:59pm ET; notifications by the end of September 2026; programme runs roughly 5 October to 18 December 2026. Contact: creatorprogram@newscreatorcorps.org. Sibling programme to the Rural Creator Fellowship.

item.title: Beinecke Library Short-Term Research Fellowships 2027-2028 (Yale)
item.description:
Organisation: Beinecke Rare Book & Manuscript Library, Yale University

Location: Onsite at Yale Library Special Collections, New Haven, Connecticut, USA. Open to academic and independent scholars locally and globally, regardless of institutional association.

Award: USD 5,000 per month for research visits between two weeks and two months. Funding is paid at the beginning of the fellowship where possible (payment to international fellows often takes several weeks); fellows are responsible for taxes on the award. Free to apply.

Duration: Two weeks to two months of onsite research, conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028; awards cannot be deferred

Deadline: Closed 15 Aug 2026

The Beinecke Library Fellowship Program offers competitive short-term fellowships to support research projects that substantively engage with Yale Library Special Collections materials. WHO CAN APPLY: academic and independent scholars, locally and globally, with or without an institutional affiliation; the library explicitly welcomes applicants regardless of institutional association, race, cultural background, ability, sexual orientation, gender or socioeconomic status. Applications using traditional archival and bibliographic research methods are encouraged, and so are creative, interdisciplinary and non-traditional approaches to working with the collections, which makes this a live option for artists and writers whose practice is research-driven. WHAT YOU GET: USD 5,000 per month for an onsite research visit of between two weeks and two months, paid at the start of the fellowship whenever possible (international fellows should expect payment to take several weeks); fellows pay their own taxes on the award. TIMELINE: applications for the 2027-2028 awards opened 1 June 2026 and close 15 August 2026, via Interfolio; all decisions are notified by 31 January 2027; research must be conducted between 1 July 2027 and 30 June 2028, and awards cannot be deferred.

item.title: Waging Nonviolence Journalism Fellowship (Fall 2026)
item.description:
Organisation: Waging Nonviolence

Location: Remote, with a flexible self-directed schedule. RESTRICTED: US-based writers.

Award: $500 initial stipend plus $250 per published story, up to $1,750 in total. No application fee.

Duration: Five months (Fall 2026), remote and self-directed; five monthly feature articles of at least 1,500 words each

Deadline: Closed 10 Aug 2026

The first Waging Nonviolence Fellowship is a five-month remote journalism programme for writers reporting on social movements, peace, justice and nonviolent action. It is framed as journalistic training: fellows work closely with senior editor Jessica Stites and editor-in-chief Eric Stoner and come out with a body of clips on an undercovered movement beat. WORK: five monthly feature articles of at least 1,500 words each for Waging Nonviolence, plus an initial meeting and check-ins as needed; fellows are expected to find their own stories, hit deadlines and respond promptly by email. PAY: a $500 stipend up front plus $250 per published story, so $1,750 across the full run. ELIGIBILITY: US-based; experience reporting on or analysing social movements; excellent writing and clean copy; genuine investment in peace and justice organising. Established connections to activist groups and communities, and knowledge of civil resistance history, theory, strategy and tactics, are preferred. APPLICATION: via a Google Form linked from the announcement; no resume or CV required. Deadline 10 August 2026. Contact: contact@wagingnonviolence.org.
